acceptanceCriteria: The generated CreateAppInput requires maintenance.authorize, the generated application passes it to the durable surface, and there is no implicit allow, ambient Admin/System Principal, browser client, Fetch route, or Operation-Wire maintenance transport.

Maintenance Authority is evaluated for the trusted Principal, exact command, and run identity before the target row is locked. A known denied target is audited, but the caller receives typed AUTHORITY_DENIED with null state and version; an unknown target returns the same shape and therefore creates no existence oracle.
acknowledgeAmbiguity, cancelRun, and retryRun each require a reason of 1 through 256 characters; invalid input is a typed, audited REASON_INVALID result and does not mutate the run.

Expected-version fencing refuses a stale caller with VERSION_MISMATCH and returns the settled current run version, which can be used for a successful retry; every non-Authority outcome reports the settled version while an Authority denial discloses none.

questpie.internal.v5 adds the nullable bounded maintenance reason to the existing append-only audit catalog, installs fresh or upgrades v4 in the pinned protocol transaction, and refuses a same-version checksum mismatch without partially accepting drift.

The generated Runtime Build declares questpie.internal.v5. A decoder test recomputes and accepts a valid v4 Runtime Build and rejects an unsupported protocol, while newly compiled applications require v5.

The maintenance tests include positive-controlled instruments proving denial precedes FOR UPDATE for each of the three commands, PostgreSQL evidence for audited denial and authorized success, all three invalid-reason paths, winner-version recovery, and durable write-guard re-arming.

The reference-local performance test executes 20 fenced maintenance commands, counts exactly their 20 audit rows, and stays under 400 ms. Readable audit SQL leaves the complete generated BETA-07 application bundle at 524,277 bytes, 11 bytes below its unchanged budget.

Studio UI, browser mounting, an inspection read model, a failed-run worklist, and ambient privileged authority remain explicit non-goals. drainRuntime remains a Runtime lifecycle operation inside Gate 8's four-command maintenance contract, and the public guide retains the accepted Runtime limit, failure, retention, and backpressure clauses.
